result.target_topic: Expansion of wafer and assembly/test facilities with recent slowdowns
result.target_summary: Intel is expanding wafer fabrication in Ireland for Intel 4/3 nodes and Arizona for Intel 18A, building a new facility in Ohio, and expanding assembly/test in New Mexico and Malaysia. However, completion of the Ohio facility has been slowed and plans for a new facility in Germany and additional expansion in Malaysia have been put on hold due to reassessed demand and capital expenditure limits.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures describe the streamlining of Intel's global manufacturing footprint in response to demand and capital constraints. D051 (2024) details the slowing of the Ohio facility, pausing of the Germany plan, and reduction of Malaysia expansion. D012 (2025) confirms these actions were executed or continued in 2025, specifically noting the consolidation of Costa Rican operations, slowing the Ohio fab, and discontinuing expansions in Germany and Poland.

current_disclosures.summary: In 2025, Intel streamlined its footprint by consolidating Costa Rican operations (expected completion by end of 2026), slowing Ohio fab construction, and discontinuing expansions in Germany and Poland. Additionally, if Intel cannot secure significant external foundry customers for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue that technology and shift manufacturing to third-party foundries like TSMC for nodes beyond Intel 18A.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company has a long history of operating in Asia, where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products and materials, and stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose significant manufacturing and inventory operations in Malaysia, but Intel is actively managing capacity adjustments there while Broadcom describes a stable, long-standing operational presence. Intel states it is 'expanding our facilities in New Mexico and Malaysia' but 'recently reduced the extent of the expansion plans for Malaysia' due to demand reassessment. In contrast, Broadcom notes it 'has a long history of operating in Asia' and 'store[s] the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia,' indicating a reliance on the location for existing operations rather than the expansion/slowdown dynamics seen at Intel.

sentences.text: We are expanding our facilities in New Mexico and Malaysia, though we recently reduced the extent of the expansion plans for Malaysia.
We store the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia and our presence in Asia places us in close proximity to many of our customers' manufacturing facilities.

peer_results.rationale: Candidates discuss global R&D center locations and product assembly/testing forms. These do not compare to Intel's specific disclosure of wafer fabrication facility expansions and the slowing of construction due to capital limits and demand reassessment.

Candidates describe a fabless strategy and supply chain concentration in Asia-Pacific. This is a fundamental business model difference (outsourced vs. owned manufacturing) and does not provide a comparable specific fact regarding the status of owned wafer fabrication facility expansions or slowdowns as disclosed by Intel.

comparisons.peer_summary: QCT uses internal fabrication facilities for certain RFFE modules and RF filter products, with front-end processes in Germany and Singapore and back-end assembly and test facilities in China and Singapore.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose specific manufacturing facilities in Germany, highlighting different strategic approaches to European manufacturing. Intel explicitly states it has 'plans for an additional new wafer production facility in Germany' but has 'put[ted] those plans... on hold' due to financial results and demand reassessment. Conversely, Qualcomm utilizes an 'internal fabrication' model where 'front-end processes primarily take place at manufacturing facilities located in Germany,' indicating active, ongoing manufacturing operations in Germany for its RFFE products, unlike Intel's paused expansion.

sentences.text: We are building a new wafer production facility in Ohio and have plans for an additional new wafer production facility in Germany, but have slowed the completion of the Ohio facility and put the plans for the facility in Germany on hold as we have reassessed demand and our "shell ahead" status and sought to limit our capital expenditures given recent financial results.

The front-end processes primarily take place at manufacturing facilities located in Germany and Singapore and involve the imprinting of substrate wafers with the structure and circuitry required for the products to function (also known as wafer fabrication).
